a:r.a:t: TPP Is a Common Acetaldehyde Carrier
TPP forms a covalent bond with carbonyl carbon, forming an alcohol, and resulting in release of CO
TPP then allows rearrangement of and protonation of carbonyl carbon to release from complex.

p:cNvPr.descr: Image (c) begins with TPP, which is a pentagon, with a double-bonded side on the top left and bottom. The left point is a positively charged N, which bonds left to R. The top point is C, which bonds up to H. The top right point is S. The bottom right point bonds down and right to R’, and the bottom left point bonds down and left to H3C. To the bottom right are reversible arrows pointing down and right. The arrow going up has H+ merging with it, and there is an arrow jetting out from the down arrow. This is step 1: C-2 in the thiazolium ring of TPP ionizes. The arrows point to TPP carbanion, which is the same as TPP, but the top point is C-. From there, a red arrow points up and right to pyruvate, where C, double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to H3C, and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. This is all in pink. A red arrow points from the double-bond line from the first C to O to H+. Below this is a down arrow. This is step 2: The TPP carbanion attacks the carbonyl group of pyruvate. Below this arrow is the same as the first pentagon described in image (c), but the top point is C, which bonds up to (all in pink) C, which bonds left to H3C, up to OH (H is black), and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. A red arrow points from the negative sign to that bond line. A red arrow also points from the bond line between C and C and points down to the bond line between the C at the top point of the pentagon and the C above. Inside the pentagon is a red arrow pointing from the top left side to N on the left point. Below this is a down arrow, which has another arrow jetting left to a red CO2. This is step 3: Decarboxylation is facilitated by electron delocalization into the thiazolium ring of TPP. Below this is a bracket where, on the left, a pentagon similar to the first pentagon in image (c) sits, but the top point is C, which bonds up to (all in pink) C (with a line above), which bonds left to H3C and right to OH (H is black). To the right of this is a double-ended arrow identified as resonance stabilization. To the right of the arrow is the same pentagon as just described, but the top point is C, which double bonds up to (all in pink) C, which bonds up and left to H3C and up and right to OH (H is black). There is a red arrow from the double bond up to C. At the left point, there are two red dots to the right of N and an arrow pointing up to the top left side. From this bracket is an up arrow on the left. On the right of the arrow, H+ merges with it. This is step 4: Protonation generated hydroxyethyl TPP. This points up to hydroxyethyl TPP. This is the same pentagon as first mentioned in image (c), but the top point has C, which bonds up to (all in pink) C. A red arrow bonds from this line back to C. The red C also bonds right to O, which bonds right to a black H. An arrow points from the bond line between O and H to the bond line between C and O. C also bonds up to a black H and left to H3C. An arrow points from the pink C up and left to acetaldehyde. This arrow has another arrow jetting off left to H+. Acetaldehyde is C, which bonds left to H3C, double bonds up and right to O (all in pink) and down and right to H. At the top and to the right is an arrow pointing up and right. This is step 5: Elimination of the thiazolium cation yields acetaldehyde. This arrow points back to step 1.
